learn.title: Small Wind Turbines Explained
learn.intro: Small wind turbines harness local wind resources to generate clean electricity for homes and communities. They reduce fossil fuel dependence while offering energy independence. Understanding their mechanics empowers rural and urban areas to adopt sustainable solutions.
learn.c1_text: Small turbines use blades to convert kinetic wind energy into mechanical rotation. A generator then transforms this into electricity. Like a pinwheel, but engineered for efficiency. Modern designs achieve 30-45% capacity factors in consistent winds.
learn.c2_text: Turbines connect to homes via inverters, converting DC to AC power. Battery storage systems store excess energy for night use. India's Ministry of New Renewable Energy supports hybrid systems combining wind and solar for 24/7 power.
learn.c3_text: India ranks 4th globally in wind capacity with 45 GW installed (2024). Tamil Nadu leads with 12 GW, leveraging monsoon-driven winds. Small turbines (<100 kW) are promoted under KUSUM scheme for farm electrification.

learn.title: Solving the Duck Curve Challenge
learn.intro: The duck curve describes grid instability when solar energy peaks midday but drops sharply at sunset. This creates urgent ramp-up needs for fossil plants. Addressing it requires storage, demand response, and smart grid innovations to ensure reliability.
learn.c1_text: Solar farms produce maximum power at noon, but clouds at dusk cause rapid output declines. Grid operators must quickly ramp up gas plants to fill gaps. In 2023, California's duck curve reached 15 GW/hour, highlighting storage needs.
learn.c2_text: Lithium-ion batteries, green hydrogen, and smart thermostats balance supply/demand. Germany uses demand-response programs where factories reduce load during sunset peaks. India's green energy corridors enhance grid stability for similar challenges.
learn.c3_text: India faces duck curve issues with 500 GW renewable target by 2030. NTPC's 2 GW battery storage projects and solar parks with hybrid storage are key steps. The 2023 Electricity Act enables flexible tariffs for managing sudden demand shifts.
learn.stat2: Germany's demand response saves 5% grid costs

learn.title: Green Bonds Finance Climate Projects
learn.intro: Green bonds are debt instruments funding climate-positive projects like solar farms and wind parks. They mobilize private capital for sustainable development. Understanding their structure reveals how trillions can be directed toward renewable energy transitions globally.
learn.c1_text: Green bonds link proceeds exclusively to environmentally beneficial projects. A third-party review verifies alignment with climate goals. The EU's taxonomy defines criteria. Over $500 billion was issued globally in 2023, with 30% funding clean energy.
learn.c2_text: Green bonds reduce financing costs by 0.5-1% compared to conventional bonds. India's Green Climate Fund bonds raised $500 million for rooftop solar. These instruments attract ESG-focused investors, accelerating project deployment at scale.
learn.c3_text: India issued $2.5 billion in green bonds in 2023 for solar and wind projects. The National Hydrogen Mission plans $1.5 billion green bonds for clean fuel infrastructure. RBI's green finance policy mandates 20% green loans by 2025.

learn.title: Microgrids Enable Energy Independence
learn.intro: Microgrids are localized energy systems combining generation, storage, and loads. They operate independently or connected to the main grid, enhancing resilience during disasters. Vital for remote communities and critical infrastructure, they represent the future of decentralized energy.
learn.c1_text: Microgrids integrate solar/wind, batteries, and smart controls. They island during outages, maintaining power to hospitals or villages. A 10 MW microgrid can serve 5,000 homes. India's 1,000 rural microgrids under Surya Mitra project demonstrate scalability.
learn.c2_text: During Hurricane Maria, Puerto Rico's microgrids restored power in hours vs weeks. In India, microgrids in Bihar provide 24/7 power to 500 villages, enabling education and healthcare. They reduce transmission losses by 15-20% locally.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 500 microgrids by 2025 under the Rural Energy Development Agency. Gujarat's 50 MW coastal microgrid combines solar, tidal, and storage. The 2023 National Microgrid Policy offers subsidies up to 30% for village-level projects.

learn.title: Green Ammonia: Clean Fuel Future
learn.intro: Green ammonia, produced via renewable-powered electrolysis, offers zero-carbon solutions for shipping and agriculture. Its versatility as fuel and fertilizer positions it as a linchpin in decarbonizing heavy industry. Global innovation is accelerating its adoption.
learn.c1_text: Green ammonia is made by splitting water into hydrogen (via renewable electricity) and combining with nitrogen from air. The process emits no CO2. A 100 MW electrolyzer produces 12,000 tons/year. IRENA estimates 150 million tons globally by 2050.
learn.c2_text: Ships can burn ammonia as fuel with modifications, reducing maritime emissions by 90%. Fertilizer production using green ammonia cuts farming's 7% global CO2 emissions. Norway's Yara Pilbara plant tests ammonia as shipping fuel in 2024 trials.
learn.c3_text: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 9 million tons/year ammonia production by 2030. PSUs like IOCL plan green ammonia plants in Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. The 2023 policy offers 30% capital subsidy for electrolyzer-based projects.

learn.title: Solar Panel Types Compared
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity through photovoltaic cells. Three main types—monocrystalline, polycrystalline, and thin-film—differ in efficiency, cost, and applications. Choosing the right panel impacts energy savings and system design for homes and businesses.
learn.c1_text: Monocrystalline panels have higher efficiency (20-22%) due to single-crystal silicon but cost 20% more. Polycrystalline panels are 15-18% efficient, cheaper, and better for limited roof space. Both use similar installation methods with inverters.
learn.c2_text: Thin-film panels (10-12% efficiency) are lightweight and flexible, ideal for curved surfaces. They degrade slower but need more space. India's desert regions use thin-film for large solar parks like Bhadla, where land is abundant and costs matter.
learn.c3_text: India's 100 GW solar target drives demand for all panel types. Monocrystalline dominates rooftop projects for efficiency. Polycrystalline is preferred for utility-scale farms. The 2023 Make in India policy aims for 30% domestic manufacturing by 2030.
